Promoting British Values
School Information
Promoting British Values
In 2014, the Department for Education published guidance on promoting British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain.
All schools have a duty to ‘actively promote’ the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
British values are outlined as:
At Mossford Green Primary School we take our responsibility to prepare our pupils for their future within modern Britain seriously. British values underpin our daily work with the children, as part of our vision, and are shared with the children through assemblies, teaching in R.E. and P.S.H.C.E. and through opportunities within our creative curriculum.
We also ensure that children are aware of their British heritage through our annual heritage day around the time of St George’s Day. On this day children explore people and places important to Britons and learn what is special about what it is to be British.
Democracy: Our children live through the democratic process each year as they vote for the new school council. Children prepare their manifestos, canvas and take part in a secret ballot to elect council members. Children can make their opinions known throughout the year through the school opinion box. These are shared in assemblies and through the school council.
Children work together in pairs, groups and whole class situations, showing respect for each other, taking turns and listening to the opinions of others.
The Rule of Law: Our ‘keeping happy and safe’ rules, written by the children of the school, enable children to understand basic rules within society. Our children develop an understanding of why law is important and the importance of respecting ourselves and others within the framework of our school community and in the wider world.
Our community police officers support the work of the school in developing a respect for the rule of law within our society.
Children are able to articulate how and why we need to behave in school and demonstrate they understand and can abide by our ‘keeping happy and safe’ rules.
Individual Liberty: Central to our vision is developing self-respect and self-worth in relation to the individual so that children see that they are important in their own right. We exemplify, through our work with the children, the right to have our own thoughts and views and the right to express these safely.
Our children are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely, e.g. through e-safety teaching, but with respect to the rights and feelings of others.
Mutual respect and tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs: Respect is deeply embedded in all that we do at the school. The pupils know and understand that respect is an expectation, shown to everyone whatever differences we may have. The core value of respect underpins our work every day both within and beyond the school community.
Within our richly diverse school community we promote a mutual understanding of and respect for, the faiths and beliefs of others. Through the locally agreed syllabus for R.E. our children learn about the major religions of the world and hear from those within the school community about how these faiths are born out in the lives of individuals. We involve our children in visits to places of worship of different faith groups to broaden their understanding.
Guest speakers further support the children’s experiences. Our children demonstrate a keen interest in learning about the lives of others and from this they develop a respect for different faiths and beliefs.

Mossford Green Primary School
Welcome from the Headteacher
I am so proud to welcome you to the Mossford Green community, where our vision is to 'make memories that last a lifetime, setting every child on course to live a life of purpose and positive impact. We empower all our children to embody our school values - being kind, creative, respectful, courageous, resilient and determined - within a culture where every child is valued and inspired to reach their full potential.'
Creativity sits at the heart of our curriculum, and ensures that children access a broad and balanced diet of learning experiences whilst building foundational skills in English, Maths and Science. Our learning is organised into learning journeys which begin with 'stunning starters' to capture the children's imagination and end with 'fabulous finishes' where they apply everything they have learnt to real world contexts. Children at Mossford Green achieve well; last year 76.7% of our pupils achieved the expected standard across Reading, Writing and Maths in KS2, compared to the national average of 62.2% and local average of 73.2%.
Our school is a joyful place, where the wellbeing of our children is at the heart of everything we do. Visitors frequently comment on the calm, positive atmosphere in the school, and on our children's impeccable manners. Our playtimes are outrageously good fun; from skateboards to den building to digging in the mud, we do it all! Where children need additional support with their wellbeing or behaviour, our award-winning emotional literacy support assistant (ELSA) team are on hand.
We are supported by a diverse community of families, and by our PTA who generously give their time and energy to support our school. Our safeguarding team ensure that all families are supported and children can come to school happy, healthy and ready to learn. The commitment to equality runs deep within our school; everyone is heard, everyone is seen, everyone is represented. We also teach our children to give back to their community; in Year 5 and 6 children complete up to 30 hours of "work in the community" as part of our Contribution to Community Award (CCA). Check out our 'community' page for more information.
But don't just take my word for it - please come and visit our wonderful school and see our children and staff in action!

Curriculum Overview
Curriculum
Curriculum Overview
Our Learning Journeys
At Mossford Green Primary School, children learn through exciting Learning Journeys that bring the curriculum to life. Each term begins with a stunning starter to spark curiosity and ends with a fabulous finish that celebrates the children’s achievements.
Our Learning Journeys link learning across the curriculum, often centred around high‑quality key texts. They are carefully planned to meet the requirements of the National Curriculum and EYFS Framework, while also reflecting the culture, interests and needs of our school community and building skills children will use for life. We aim to make learning memorable, meaningful and enjoyable.
Wherever possible, children learn through hands‑on experiences, including educational visits, workshops and opportunities to work with visiting experts. We also value contributions from parents and families who can enrich our topics with their own knowledge and experiences.
While English and Mathematics (including phonics and reading) are taught discretely, we make meaningful links to our Learning Journeys whenever appropriate.
We teach Religious Education in line with the Redbridge Agreed Syllabus, promoting understanding and respect for different faiths. Our PSHCE curriculum has been updated to meet statutory RSHE guidance introduced in 2020.
For more detailed information on our learning journeys, please see our Curriculum Map and the relevant year group.
You may also find the following links helpful:

For subject‑specific information, please visit our Early Years and Key Stage One & Two pages.

Mossford Green Primary School
Pupils
Assessments
Children are nationally assessed to ascertain their progress within school; they are assessed at 5 points throughout their time in primary school.
Reception pupils undertake a baseline assessment within the first 6 weeks of starting school, they then are assessed against the Early Learning Goals (ELG) at the end of the Reception year. More information can be found at this link.
Year One pupils will take part in the Statutory Phonics Screening check, which checks their ability to decode words. They complete the screen again in Year Two, if they don’t reach the expected standard in year one. More information can be found at this link.
Year Four pupils will take part in the statutory multiplication check, which checks their ability to recall multiplication facts up to 12x12, at speed. More information can be found at this link.
Year Six pupils will sit the Standardised tests: Standard Attainment Tests (SATs) .
In Key Stage 2, the tests are more formal and school-level results are published in the national performance tables (League tables) allowing for comparison with other schools. Children will sit tests in reading; grammar, punctuation and spelling and Maths. They will also be formally assed by their teacher in writing and science. More information can be found at this link.
Teachers and the Leadership Team continuously monitor progress through ongoing observations, discussions and informal tests. Staff can use this information to indicate progress being made, to adapt teaching, planning and to review and analyse the curriculum, if needed.
Children are given timely feedback about their performance with the aim of helping them to set targets.

At Mossford Green, we are continuing to develop links with our community and ensuring that are children see the strength in supporting one another both in and outside of school. Operation Mossford Magic
Thank you to all of the school community for all of your amazing donations. Our group of Year 6 children were able to create just over 50 parcels that were collected by Redbridge Foodbank to give out to children most in need over the festive season. We are so proud!
CCA - Contribution to Community Award
The CCA is a unique opportunity for the children in our year 5 and 6 to develop themselves. They will use develop skills to contribute to the community around them. By using these they will be able to earn Bronze, then Silver and finally, their Gold award.
They will be able to achieve these by thinking about the different sections of the community.

There are so many opportunities outside of the school gates where we can contribute within Barkingside and the Borough of Redbridge. When we look around at the community, we have to think about what we can do to help and support. E.g. Taking part in community events or doing a litter pick in our local park.
The world is ever changing and being part of a wider community is so important as we grow up. We have to keep looking out at the world around us and think about how we can help (even just as individuals!) E.g. Fundraising for disasters or charities, thinking of ways to look after the environment.

Phonics at Mossford Green Primary School
We ensure that the teaching of reading focuses on developing children’s skills in:
· Comprehension (both listening and reading)
It is essential that, by the end of their primary education, all pupils can read fluently and with confidence, so that they are empowered for their future education and for life.
We also want children to develop a love of reading through immersion in a variety of text types.
To ensure children become skilled readers, we:
1.) Have a whole-school systematic phonics programme
Since September 2026, we have been using the government-validated systematic synthetic phonics (SSP) programme called Little Wandle: Letters & Sounds Revised.
The programme is designed to teach children to read from Reception to Year 2, using the skills of decoding and blending sounds together to form words.
“The Little Wandle programme provides a full progression through all commonly occurring GPCs* (sounds), working from simple to more complex, and taking into account the frequency of their occurrence in the most commonly encountered words.” Please visit the Little Wandle website for more information. The ‘For Parents’ section provides videos demonstrating how to pronounce the Phase 2 and Phase 3 sounds and how we teach children to read words. https://www.littlewandle.org.uk/resources/for-parents/
2.) Send reading books home
Books for sharing are sent home for families to enjoy together, helping to develop a love of reading.
Reception and Year 1
Key words are sent home once introduced in class. Children are sent home with reading books from the Little Wandle scheme that match the sounds taught.
They also bring home books for sharing with their families to foster a love of reading.
Some children who are continuing with the Little Wandle scheme will continue to bring home reading books matched to the sounds they have learned. Children who have completed the Little Wandle programme and passed the phonics screening check will bring home reading books matched to their reading ability following the Little Wandle fluency programme until they are ready to be a free reader.
Children continue to take home sight words to practise. They also bring home books for sharing with their families to encourage a love of reading.
Children in KS2 continue to bring home books matched to their reading ability if they have not finished the phonics programme. Once they become Free Readers, they are able to choose books that interest them.
We encourage children not to change their books unless they can show that they have read and understood the current one.﻿

Mossford Green Primary School
Mossford Green Primary School
Reading for Pleasure
Curriculum
Reading for Pleasure
Reading is the foundation of all learning
Reading Vision
At Mossford Green Primary School , children understand that reading opens doors for them. It helps them to stand in the shoes of hundreds of other people. To live a thousand different lives. Children know that reading helps them to improve their language and vocabulary skills. That reading better equips them to be successful in all areas of learning throughout their education.
We strive to give all children a life-long love of reading, as well as to develop the skills they need to prepare them for the next stage of their journeys.
How We Teach Reading at Mossford Green
Reading is the foundation of all learning at Mossford Green. In Nursery, this begins with reading exciting books as a class, reading and singing nursery rhymes and the teaching of early phonics. By the time children are in reception, each child will have a colour banded book closely matching their phonics skills. Children will read one-to-one with an adult and discuss the book they are reading. Quality books will also be the basis of their learning in of all key areas and systematic phonics teaching continues daily with targeted interventions for groups and individuals.
In year 1, children continue to learn decoding skills through daily phonics teaching, as well as reading one-to-one with an adult. Children also have 15 minutes per day to read to themselves. Children also focus on quality texts in small groups with a teacher where they discuss vocabulary, inference and retrieval questions.
By the time the children are in year 2 and throughout KS2, children will begin studying books in depth as a whole class for 25 minutes per day. In these whole class reading sessions, the children will explore deeper questions about a text, including discussions based on a range of issues e.g. semantic, intratextual, narratological, prosodic foci. This is in addition to an hour of daily English teaching where reading may also be the focus. Children will continue to read their own book to themselves for 15 minutes per day as well.
This means that every child will have at least 40 minutes of reading focus every day.
As well as book corners in every classroom, the school also has a well stocked library that all the children visit on a fortnightly basis. The children also visit our local library, Fullwell cross Library, every six weeks to choose a book.
Diversity
At Mossford Green, we are passionate about the characters and authors reflecting our diverse community. That is why we have heavily invested in books with BAME characters for all our classrooms and our library.
﻿We are constantly looking for new books and authors that will appeal to all our children and encourage our parents, carers and children to make suggestions!
Looking For Your Next Exciting Read at Home?
We know that choosing a great book can be tricky, so we have made suggestions for each year group. Please click on the appropriate year below then have a look at the books we suggest. We’d love your suggestions too!

Safeguarding
School Information
Safeguarding and Child Protection
At Mossford Green we are committed to safeguarding every child within our school.
If you have any concerns over a child or young person's health or welfare; of being harmed through abuse or neglect; please speak to the school's Designated Safeguarding Leaders Miss H. Birkett (Deputy Headteacher) or Mr M. Tranter (Headteacher).
Or you can contact Redbridge’s Children's Social Care Team on Tel: 020 8708 3885 or
e-mail: CPAT.referrals@redbridge.gov.uk.
During the evening or at weekends, please call the Emergency Duty Team on 020 8708 5897.
For more information visit Redbridge's Child Protection website
In emergency situations please contact the Police on 999.
The NSPCC Helpline can be contacted for advice on 0808 800 5000.
Operation Encompass
At Mossford Green Primary we work in partnership with the Metropolitan Police and Children’s Services to identify and provide appropriate support to pupils who have experienced domestic violence in their household; this scheme is called Operation Encompass.
The purpose of Operation Encompass is to safeguard and support children and young people who have been involved in or witness to a domestic abuse incident. Domestic abuse impacts on children in a number of ways. Children are at increased risk of physical injury during an incident, either by accident or because they attempt to intervene. Even when not directly injured, children are greatly distressed by witnessing the physical and emotional suffering of a parent.
Encompass has been created to highlight this situation. It is the implementation of key partnership working between the police and schools. The aim of sharing information with local schools is to allow ‘Key Adults/Safeguarding lead’ the opportunity of engaging with the child and to provide access to support that allows them to remain in a safe but secure familiar environment.
In order to achieve this, the Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub will share police information of all domestic incidents where one of our pupils has been present, with the Designated Safeguarding Lead(s) (DSL). On receipt of any information, the DSL will decide on the appropriate support the child requires, this should be covert dependent on the needs and wishes of the child.
All information sharing and resulting actions will be undertaken in accordance with the Metropolitan Police and MASH Encompass Protocol Data Sharing Agreement. We will record this information and store this information in accordance with the record keeping procedures outlined in our school's Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy.
